result:
Lint passes clean, 0 violations. Both test suites pass fully. Summary of the change:

- `crates/ucal/src/clock.rs`: added `anchor_at_start()`, which anchors the process-wide session clock (idempotently, reusing the existing `session_now` machinery) and updated the surrounding docs to reflect that the session is now anchored at program start rather than lazily on first use; added a unit test verifying the anchor doesn't move on a second call.
- `crates/ucal/src/main.rs`: calls `ucal::clock::anchor_at_start()` as the first thing in `main`, before argument parsing/dispatch, so the anchor reflects when the process started (notably fixing the case where `-`/stdin streaming reads all input before the first "now" would otherwise have been requested). The call is best-effort — a failure surfaces normally the first time a command actually needs the clock, so commands that never read time aren't newly made fragile.

`cargo test -q -p ucal --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -q -p xtask --no-fail-fast` both pass, and `xtask lint` reports 0 violations. Not committed, per your instructions.
